title: JavaScript Fundamentals
description: Types, scope, async, and the array methods you reach for daily.

questions.explanation: A longstanding bug kept for backwards compatibility: null's type tag is the object tag.

questions.prompt: topScores should return the three highest scores without changing the caller's array — but afterwards scores[0] is 97. Click the buggy line.
questions.explanation: sort() sorts in place and returns the same array, so the caller's scores gets reordered. Copy first — [...scores].sort(...) — or use scores.toSorted(...).

questions.prompt: `const` prevents the contents of an object from being changed.
questions.explanation: const binds the variable, not the value — you can still mutate the object it points at.

questions.prompt: Which of these values are falsy in JavaScript? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: An empty array is an object, and all objects are truthy. 0, "", and NaN are falsy.

questions.prompt: What does an `async` function always return?
questions.explanation: An async function wraps its return value in a Promise, even if you return a plain value.

questions.prompt: Put the lines in order so activeEmails returns the emails of active users only.
questions.explanation: filter has to come before map: once you've mapped to email strings, there's no `active` field left to filter on.
With a string operand, + concatenates, so "5" + 3 is "53". Minus has no string meaning, so "5" - 3 coerces to numbers and gives 2.

questions.prompt: What does this log, in order?
questions.explanation: == coerces: "" becomes 0, so 0 == "" is true. === never coerces, so a number and a string are never equal. null == undefined is a special case that is true (but null === undefined is false).

questions.prompt: cartTotal should return 30, but it returns "[object Object]20". Click the buggy line.
questions.explanation: With no initial value, reduce uses the first ITEM as the starting sum — an object — and object + number concatenates as strings. Pass a starting value: reduce((sum, item) => ..., 0).

questions.prompt: An arrow function has its own `this` binding.
questions.explanation: Arrow functions inherit `this` from the enclosing scope — that's the main reason to use one in a callback.

questions.prompt: Which of these create a new array or object rather than modifying the original? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Object.assign mutates its first argument. Spread, slice, and filter all produce something new.

questions.prompt: In what order are the letters logged?
questions.explanation: Synchronous code runs first (A, D). Then the microtask queue drains — promise callbacks like C — before the next macrotask, which is the setTimeout callback B. A 0ms timeout still waits its turn.

questions.prompt: Put the lines in order so getJson throws on an HTTP error and otherwise returns the parsed body.
questions.explanation: fetch only rejects on network failure — a 404 or 500 still resolves. So you check res.ok yourself, before parsing, and throw if it's false.
find() returns undefined when nothing matches, and reading .name off undefined throws "Cannot read properties of undefined". Guard with user?.name or check the result first.

questions.prompt: loadUserName always returns undefined, even for users that exist. Click the buggy line.
questions.explanation: res.json() returns a Promise, not the parsed object. Without await, user is a Promise and user.name is undefined. Fix: const user = await res.json();
